summary: First checkpoint: the real vector space of height functions modulo uniformly bounded functions, its contravariant pullback, and invariance of native Northcott finiteness under bounded error. The bounded-function submodule, quotient algebra and finite-fiber Northcott theorem are imported from Mathlib. The geometric height machine, canonical heights and RP.1–RP.6 are not claimed complete.

sources.title: Notes on Heights
sources.edition: Undated author-hosted course notes, linked by the Spring 2022 Schemes course page; 13-page copy accessed 2026-09-27
readSections: Read physical/printed pp.1–3 and 6–10: goals and elementary heights; coordinate estimates; all of §14, including its footnote and Steps 1–7; local-function discussion and §17. Pages 4–5 and 11–13 are not claimed read. Pages 2,6,8,9 were visually checked for the recorded source findings. The quotient and finiteness interfaces below use §14 footnote and §17 as motivation, with their elementary proofs written here. No claim that the notes prove the complete roadmap.

Authorship and course context verified at https://www.math.columbia.edu/~dejong/courses/schemes-spring-2022.html. No dated revision or separate correction located on that page or the author homepage on 2026-09-27.

nodes.title: Uniform boundedness at the top filter
nodes.statement: For h:X→ℝ, membership in the native boundedFilterSubmodule at the top filter is equivalent to the existence of C≥0 such that |h(x)|≤C for every x∈X.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Unfold native boundedFilterSubmodule and BoundedAtFilter. Asymptotics.isBigO_top changes the filter statement into one bound for every x, since the norm of the constant real one is one.
Replace a possibly negative bound C by max(C,0). This also handles X empty without a nonemptiness assumption. Conversely forget nonnegativity and use the native top-filter equivalence.
acceptance: On the empty type C=0 works.
The alternating sequence (−1)^n has bound 1.
The sequence n on the natural numbers has no uniform bound.

sources.match: Elementary quotient interface extracted from the source’s height-class convention; the proof uses the listed native declarations.

nodes.title: Heights modulo bounded functions
nodes.statement: For any type X, HeightClass(X) is the native real module quotient of the function space X→ℝ by Filter.boundedFilterSubmodule at the top filter. Write [h] for the native linear quotient projection. It is a real vector space; no topology or pointwise evaluation of a class is supplied.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Specialize the native bounded-function submodule to real-valued functions and the top filter, then use the native submodule quotient. This is a transparent abbreviation, not another quotient relation or another boundedness predicate.

Use the inherited quotient module structure and mkQ. Constants belong to the submodule by const_boundedAtFilter, so their classes vanish. On a finite type every real function has a finite, hence bounded, range. The native metric boundedness criterion at center zero gives the Bornology compatibility statement.
For linear descent use native liftQ with the exact kernel-inclusion hypothesis; liftQ_apply and quot_hom_ext supply its computation and uniqueness interfaces.
acceptance: Bounded nonconstant functions vanish.
A pointwise product of two classes is not defined: [1]=[0], but [n·1]≠[n·0].
Finite point sets give the zero quotient.

sources.match: Elementary quotient interface extracted from the source’s height-class convention; the proof uses the listed native declarations.

uses.how: Additivity and difference of very ample presentations are exact equalities in this quotient.
Pullback of line bundles requires precomposition on this quotient.
The bounded-error convention identifies input representatives. The analytic limit remains the DY.1 owner; no convergence theorem is claimed here.
Native Northcott finiteness must be independent of the representative chosen for a geometric height.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.mk
api.statement: The projection h↦[h] is exactly native mkQ, as a real linear map from functions to HeightClass(X).

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.mk_eq_mk_iff_isBounded
api.statement: [h]=[g] exactly when the range of h−g is Bornology.IsBounded in ℝ.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.mk_eq_zero_iff
api.statement: [h]=0 exactly when there is C≥0 with |h(x)|≤C for every x.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.mk_surjective
api.statement: Every height class has a real-valued function representative.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.mk_zero
api.statement: The class of the zero function is zero.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.mk_const
api.statement: For every real c, the class of the constant function with value c is zero.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.mk_of_finite
api.statement: If X is finite, every function h:X→ℝ has zero class.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.liftQ_mk
api.statement: If L:(X→ℝ)→V is a real linear map annihilating the native bounded-function submodule, its native liftQ evaluated at [h] is L(h).

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.linearMap_ext
api.statement: Two real linear maps from HeightClass(X) to V are equal if they agree on [h] for every function h.

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.tests.alternating

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.tests.unbounded

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.tests.affine_shift

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.tests.native_quotient

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.tests.not_constants_only

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.tests.not_ring_quotient

nodes.title: The bounded-error equality criterion
nodes.statement: For h,g:X→ℝ, [h]=[g] if and only if there is a real C≥0 such that |h(x)−g(x)|≤C for every x.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use native Submodule.Quotient.eq to replace equality by membership of h−g in the bounded-function submodule.
Apply uniform-boundedness and evaluate subtraction pointwise. The bound is uniform over the whole chosen point type, not merely pointwise finite or bounded on a separately chosen finite subset.
acceptance: [2n]≠[n] on ℕ.
Equality of classes does not imply equality of values at a point.

sources.match: Elementary quotient interface extracted from the source’s height-class convention; the proof uses the listed native declarations.

nodes.title: Pullback of height classes
nodes.statement: For any function f:X→Y, pullback(f):HeightClass(Y)→HeightClass(X) is the real linear map induced by precomposition: [h]↦[h∘f]. For X→Y→Z, pullback(g∘f)=pullback(f)∘pullback(g). No finite-fiber assumption is needed to define this map.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Form the native precomposition linear map from LinearMap.pi and LinearMap.proj: its x-coordinate is evaluation at f(x).
If h is bounded by C everywhere on Y, h∘f has the same bound on X. By uniform-boundedness this is exactly the submodule compatibility required by native mapQ.

Use native mapQ with that compatibility proof. Its evaluation, identity and composition theorems give the representative formula and contravariant functor laws. Constant f produces a constant representative, hence the zero map.
acceptance: On ℕ, pullback of [n] along doubling is 2[n].
Pullback along a constant map is zero.
Composition reverses order.

sources.match: Elementary quotient interface extracted from the source’s height-class convention; the proof uses the listed native declarations.

uses.how: The tensor-compatible height assignment is contravariant under maps on rational points.
A self-map acts on the bounded-error input class; the condition of being an eigenclass is independent of representatives.
Restriction to a subset of points, and the point maps induced by morphisms, use the same pullback construction.

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.pullback_id
api.statement: Pullback of the identity on X is the identity linear map on HeightClass(X).

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.pullback_comp
api.statement: For f:X→Y and g:Y→Z, pullback(g∘f)=pullback(f) composed with pullback(g).

api.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.pullback_const
api.statement: For any y∈Y, pullback of the constant map X→Y with value y is the zero linear map.

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.pullback_tests.double
tests.statement: Pullback of [n] along n↦2n on ℕ is 2[n].

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.pullback_tests.constant
tests.statement: Pullback of [n] along the constant zero map ℕ→ℕ is zero.

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.pullback_tests.composition
tests.statement: Pullback of [n²] along doubling after successor is pullback along successor of pullback along doubling of [n²].

tests.name: TauCeti.HeightClass.pullback_tests.noninjective
tests.statement: Pullback along the constant zero map ℕ→ℕ is not injective.

nodes.title: Surjective maps detect height classes
nodes.statement: If f:X→Y is surjective, pullback(f):HeightClass(Y)→HeightClass(X) is injective.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Choose representatives h and g for two classes, using native mkQ_surjective. The definition through mapQ says equality of pullbacks is equality of [h∘f] and [g∘f].
Use equality-criterion to obtain C bounding |h(f(x))−g(f(x))| on all X. For each y choose an x with f(x)=y; the same C bounds the difference on Y.
Apply equality-criterion on Y. No finiteness of the fibers is used.
acceptance: A bijection gives an isomorphism through its inverse pullback.
Projection ℕ×ℕ→ℕ is surjective and detects classes even though it does not preserve Northcott finiteness.

sources.match: Elementary consequence of the source’s bounded-error and pullback convention; not attributed as a separately stated source theorem.

nodes.title: Northcott transfer under a lower comparison
nodes.statement: Let h,g:X→ℝ and C∈ℝ satisfy h(x)≤g(x)+C for every x. If h is Northcott in the native sense, then g is Northcott.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Fix a real B. If g(x)≤B, then h(x)≤B+C. Thus the B-sublevel set of g is a subset of the (B+C)-sublevel set of h.
Apply native Northcott.finite_le and finite-set subset closure. This constructs the native Northcott instance for g; it introduces no second finiteness predicate.
acceptance: Take h(n)=n and g(n)=n+(−1)^n, with C=1.
The reversed inequality is insufficient: 0≤n on ℕ, while n is Northcott and the constant zero function is not.

sources.match: Explicit elementary sublevel-set proof supplying the representative interface for the finiteness notion used by the source. No projective Northcott theorem is re-planned.

nodes.title: Northcott invariance under bounded error
nodes.statement: If h,g:X→ℝ have equal height classes, then native Northcott(h) holds if and only if native Northcott(g) holds.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Use equality-criterion to choose C≥0 with |h(x)−g(x)|≤C for every x. The absolute-value inequality gives both h(x)≤g(x)+C and g(x)≤h(x)+C.
Apply northcott-one-sided to each comparison. Both implications use the same C; no representative selection is part of the resulting statement.
acceptance: n and n+(−1)^n on ℕ both have finite sublevel sets.
n and −n on ℕ are not boundedly equivalent; only the first is Northcott.

On a fixed field, this transfers an imported arithmetic-height finiteness theorem to any boundedly equal geometric representative. It does not assert finiteness over an algebraic closure without a degree restriction.

sources.match: Combines the source’s bounded-error convention with the native finite-sublevel definition by the displayed two inclusions.

nodes.title: Northcott for a boundedly equal pullback
nodes.statement: Let f:X→Y have finite fibers, in the native TendstoCofinite sense. Let h:Y→ℝ be Northcott and g:X→ℝ satisfy [g]=pullback(f)([h]). Then g is Northcott.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are arbitrary types, with no topology or nonemptiness assumption; all functions take real values. Additional assumptions are stated explicitly.
proofSteps: Native Northcott.comp_of_finite_fibers gives Northcott(h∘f); use the native finite-fiber typeclass and its singleton-fiber characterization.
The mapQ representative formula rewrites the hypothesis as [g]=[h∘f]. Apply northcott-invariance. This only adds the bounded-error bridge; the finite-fiber theorem is imported.
acceptance: For projection ℕ×Fin(2)→ℕ and h(n)=n, the pullback has finite sublevels.
For projection ℕ×ℕ→ℕ, the zero-sublevel set contains all (0,m), so finite fibers cannot be omitted.

sources.match: A reusable consequence of pullback and finite-sublevel finiteness, explicitly built on the native finite-fiber result. It assumes no unstated ampleness or arithmetic theorem.

remaining: The geometric height-machine construction: Construct the map from actual Picard classes of projective varieties to HeightClass of their chosen rational or algebraic point type. Read and decompose the Segre and coordinate-change bounds, the globally generated comparison, very ample difference presentations and their independence. Match the existing invertible-sheaf and Picard suppliers before writing signatures. This checkpoint gives the target vector space, not that map. The §14 Step 7 bridge is recorded in sourceIssues.

Absolute normalization and geometric Northcott applications: Import the reviewed arithmetic-height baseline and establish its precise projective and scheme-point comparison, field-extension normalization, degree restrictions and ampleness hypotheses. Native Northcott here is only the generic finite-sublevel property. No finiteness on the full algebraic closure is asserted.

Canonical and local heights on general abelian varieties: Read complete primary proofs, import ArithmeticDynamics:DY.1/tate-limit for the analytic limit, and supply the symmetric-line-bundle multiplication identity, uniqueness, quadratic polarization, local/global compatibility and comparison with the pinned elliptic half-x-height. Inspect actual pairing and regulator normalization. GZ.1/GZ.2 overlap is recorded as an ownership proposal, not a second construction.

General abelian Kummer geometry and finite generation: Decompose actual isogeny and fppf Kummer maps and the geometric realization of the protected elliptic-anchor abstract Selmer structures. Prove finite quotients and the height descent to finite generation, and compare the elliptic example to the existing explicit descent. Do not interpret a Selmer bound as an exact rank.

Adelic evaluation and unramified finite support: Read Poonen Chapter 8 and the Harpaz–Wittenberg source fully. Construct actual scheme adelic points, Brauer evaluation and the carrier comparison to ClassFieldTheory Layers 5/10 invariants and global reciprocity. For the unramified pairing use the full product of local points and prove finite support there; a restricted adelic carrier cannot replace it without comparison.

Brauer constants and almost-everywhere local triviality: Process PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23 items 29,31,38,61: unramified Brauer classes, actual image Br₀, Br₁/Br₀, and Bω as almost-everywhere trivial localization in Brauer quotients. Do not replace this condition by constancy of evaluation functions. Prove diagonal-point orthogonality via the actual invariant maps, and the finite-subgroup tests.

Torsor descent and comparison of obstructions: Read Poonen §§6.5–6.9 and §9.5 and construct twists, stabilizers, local lifts and the precise equality/inclusion of obstruction sets under stated hypotheses. Reuse the elliptic twist and Weil–Châtelet specializations from the protected anchor. A scheme or torsor carrier must not be replaced by a proposition.

Parshin and Siegel proof decompositions: Read complete proof sources for uniformly bounded Parshin covers, ramification and field extensions. Import the R28.5 Shafarevich owner. Decompose Siegel with exact genus/boundary and DiophantineApproximation DT.2 input. Distinguish finite sets from effective height bounds or enumeration algorithms.

Mordell–Lang and Manin–Mumford: Acquire and read complete primary proofs with characteristic and field hypotheses, define the actual stabilizers and translates, and decompose finitely generated subgroup and torsion intersections. Positive-dimensional torsion translates remain valid infinite components.

Bogomolov and small-point equidistribution: Acquire and decompose the complete Ullmo/Zhang proofs for the number-field small-points theorem. Symmetric ampleness, the positive threshold and failure of Zariski density must be explicit; torsion classification and R28 finiteness do not prove this conclusion. Reconcile the ArithmeticDynamics DY.4 equidistribution owner.

Classification interfaces and frontier register: RP.6 is a process layer in the reviewed audit but was not dropped by accepted RS-03. Keep its coverage open until its interfaces, actual Jacobian point-transfer statements and worked genus cases are specified, or the maintainer accepts the rescope proposal. Conjectures must have no proved-result consumers.

sourceIssues.reason: Fact II gives difference presentations of arbitrary invertible modules; Fact III says that tensoring a very ample bundle with a globally generated one is very ample.

sourceIssues.locator: §14, Step 7, p.9 in the undated 13-page author copy read 2026-09-27
sourceIssues.correction: Insert the globally generated comparison: tensor a globally generated L by a sufficiently positive very ample N as in Fact IV; the Segre identity gives the height of its chosen generating sections as h(L⊗N)−h(N). Additivity identifies this with h(L). Apply this comparison to both L and f*L before asserting pullback.
sourceIssues.reason: Step 3 only states the comparison for very ample L. A pullback of a very ample bundle can be trivial under a constant morphism and need not be very ample, so the cited step alone does not justify its second use.

sourceIssues.locator: §15, equation (15.0.1), p.9 in the undated 13-page author copy read 2026-09-27
sourceIssues.correction: Use log(max{1,||1+a||ᵥ}) in the sum if this is the height comparison for [1:1+a]. Alternatively restrict a≠−1 and state an extended-log convention if only the weaker untruncated inequality is intended. The max version is the one supplied by Axiom 2.
sourceIssues.reason: At a=−1 each displayed logarithm has zero argument. With the usual real logarithm this is undefined; the projective height itself is well defined and equals zero. The pointwise estimate (15.0.2) is meaningful at a=−1.

Have GZ.1 import those general foundations and retain Poincaré, polarization and coefficient-field comparisons specific to Gross–Zagier.
